1. A git.exe in the working folder runs on Windows 🐞 Bug ⭐ New
>
>Description >
> >
>readOriginRemote() calls execFileSync('git', …) with a bare command name, and on Windows Node's
>process spawner (libuv search_path) looks for git.com/git.exe in the current directory before
>it searches PATH. On Windows, running tracenotes render --origin inside a cloned or downloaded
>tree that contains git.exe or git.com at its root runs that file instead of the installed git,
>so the tool executes untrusted code and its output comes from that program, while on Linux the same
>command resolves only through PATH.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/cli.ts[R143-148]](https://github.com/UBayouski/tracenotes/pull/26/files#diff-fa8d4e24d8399e8350f1c8bad05df53e8032ea995835bf911507015e2db61cddR143-R148) > >```diff >+function readOriginRemote(): string { >+ return execFileSync('git', ['remote', 'get-url', 'origin'], { >+ encoding: 'utf8', >+ stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'], >+ windowsHide: true, >+ }); >``` >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >On Windows, `execFileSync('git', ...)` in `readOriginRemote()` resolves `git` from the current directory before `PATH` (libuv `search_path`). A `git.exe` or `git.com` in the working directory therefore runs when the user passes `--origin`. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/cli.ts[139-149] > >## Recommended Fix >Use Node built-ins only, with no new dependency. Before the spawn, on `process.platform === 'win32'`, set `process.env.NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath = '1'`. libuv calls `NeedCurrentDirectoryForExePathW`, which reads the parent process's environment, so this skips the cwd lookup. Another option is to walk `process.env.PATH` yourself with `path.delimiter`, `fs.existsSync` and the `.exe` extension, then pass the absolute path to `execFileSync`. Add a comment explaining why. If practical, add a Windows-only test that puts a dummy `git.exe` in a temp cwd and asserts it is not run. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

3. Git settings can break origin tests 🐞 Bug
>
>Description >
> >
>isolatedGitEnv() removes GIT_* variables but retains the caller’s global Git configuration,
>while the child-process assertions expect GitHub URLs unchanged. If that configuration rewrites
>git@github.com: with url.*.insteadOf, git remote get-url origin returns the rewritten URL and
>the otherwise-correct origin test fails.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[tests/cli.test.ts[R651-654]](https://github.com/UBayouski/tracenotes/pull/26/files#diff-ef57525fc93b3a3cf24db85f90504251c4d3cd3605b32682e8508fce02b06cafR651-R654) > >```diff >+ const isolatedGitEnv = (source: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): NodeJS.ProcessEnv => ({ >+ ...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(source).filter(([name]) => !name.toUpperCase().startsWith('GIT_'))), >+ GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES: base, >+ }); >``` >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The temporary-repository tests inherit user and system Git configuration, so an `insteadOf` rule can change the URL returned by Git and break fixed-URL assertions. >## Fix Focus Areas >- tests/cli.test.ts[648-663] >- tests/cli.test.ts[674-689] >## Recommended Fix >Give both the setup Git commands and CLI child processes an isolated, portable home and Git configuration environment. Disable system configuration for these tests, while preserving the production reader’s intended behavior. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
